title: Laser microirradiation as a tool to investigate the role of liquid-liquid phase separation in DNA damage repair
protocol: Trypsinize, count and plate 200,000 HeLa cells per well onto 6-well plates or 3.5 cm Petri dishes in cell culture medium.
Transfect cells using ∼ 1 μg plasmid DNA and 2–3 μL Lipofectamine 2000 diluted in OptiMEM to a final volume of 500 μL from 18 to 24 h after plating.
Trypsinize, count and plate 100,000 transfected cells onto glass-bottom 3.5 cm Petri dishes from 18 to 24 h after transfection.
Allow cells to express GFP-tagged proteins for at least 36–48 h after transfection for optimal cell imaging.
Prepare cell culture medium for microirradiation the day after plating transfected cells onto glass-bottom Petri dishes.
Add 0.5 μg of Hoechst per milliliter of culture medium (diluted from stock at 1:2000).
Remove the medium from the Petri dish.
Add 2 mL of phenol-red free medium containing Hoechst.
Draw seven square ROIs and three rectangular ROIs in NIS-Elements software.
Right-click the rectangular ROIs and set them to "Bleaching ROIs".
Adjust the size of bleaching ROIs, setting their height to 5 pixels.
In “Acquisition”, select the desired brightness.
Set “Scan Size” to 512 × 512-pixels or 1024 × 1024-pixels in “Scan settings”.
Set “Scan speed” to fast and “Count” to 2.
Set “Zoom” to 5.
Select the 405 nm laser and set its power to 5–25% under "Photo Activation/Bleaching".
Choose “HV mode during stimulation” as “Keep HV”.
Set “Scan Speed” to 4 s per frame (pixel dwell 12.4 μs).
Select “Applications” and “ND stimulation”.
Define three phases in the "ND stimulation" tab: Acquisition, Stimulation, and another Acquisition phase.
Set Acquisition phase to take three baseline images with 3 loops.
Select all stimulation ROIs for the Stimulation phase with only 1 loop.
Configure the second Acquisition phase to take 180 images within 3 minutes (one image per second).
Select "Perform Time Measurement" and “Apply Stimulation Settings” in the ND stimulation tab.
Click "Run now".
Save the file once irradiation is finished.
Export data to an Excel table from the "Time Measurement" tab.
Turn on the confocal microscope, the 405 nm laser (total power output of 405.7 mW), and the acquisition software.
Maintain cells in a humidified chamber at 37°C and 5% CO2 during irradiation (set 0.03 L/min of CO2 flow for 0.6 L/min air flow).
Change medium containing Hoechst with fresh phenol red-free medium after 30 minutes to avoid excessive sensitization.
Add 3 rectangular Regions of Interest (ROIs) on the live imaging screen.
Add 7 square ROIs on the live imaging screen.
Set the rectangular ROIs as “Bleaching ROIs” with a height of 5 pixels and variable length.
Use six square ROIs for bleaching control during imaging over time.
Designate one square ROI as the background control.
Adjust cell size to determine the size of the square ROIs, ensuring adequate spacing between them.
Avoid placing ROIs over nucleoli or intense GFP granules.
Use a 60× objective with a numerical aperture of 1.4 and oil immersion.
Set digital zoom at 5× for imaging.
Configure image resolution to 512 × 512 pixels if assessing one picture per second.
Choose a higher resolution of 1024 × 1024 pixels if fewer timepoints are assessed, such as one picture every 30 seconds.
Set scan speed to Fast: 2 frames/s with a pixel dwell of 0.7 μs for lower resolution images.
Select a slower scan speed of 0.5 frames/s with a pixel dwell of 1.1 μs for higher resolution images.
Perform line averaging by setting count to 2, resulting in an average of two images per timepoint.
Navigate to the “Photo Activation/Bleaching” page.
Activate only the 405 nm laser and set power between 5% and 25%, corresponding to a range of 20.3–101.4 mW.
Choose Keep HV mode during stimulation with HV linear correction.
Apply the same settings for additional stimulation areas if multiple cells are irradiated simultaneously.
Set scan speed to 4 seconds per frame, ensuring a pixel dwell time of 12.4 μs.
Sensitize cells with Hoechst for 30 min prior to laser microirradiation experiment.
Initiate the laser microirradiation after cell sensitization.
Acquire images for apical proteins (e.g., KU80) for 3 minutes, taking one photo per second.
Acquire images for other proteins (e.g., FUS) for 5 minutes, taking one photo every 30 seconds.
Acquire images for downstream/effector proteins (e.g., 53BP1) for 15 minutes, taking one photo per minute.
Select one “Bleaching ROI” for laser microirradiation.
Irradiate only one cell at a time using the selected ROI.
Perform “Time measurement” after finishing the acquisition.
Export data and proceed to data analysis.
Fix Petri dishes with 4% PFA immediately after irradiation to demonstrate DSB formation.
Stain cells for γH2AX or another DNA damage marker using a standardized immunofluorescence protocol.
Image stained cells immediately after staining.
If immediate imaging is not possible, fill dishes with PBS and cover with aluminum foil in the fridge.
Mix 1,6-Hexanediol with the cell culture medium to perturb liquid-liquid phase separation.
Use 2,5-Hexanediol as a negative control by mixing it with the cell culture medium without affecting liquid-liquid phase separation.
Add ammonium acetate to the cell culture medium to inhibit RNA-protein gelation without altering intracellular pH.
Remove the medium from the Petri dish.
Add 2 mL of phenol-red free medium containing both the treatment of choice and Hoechst.
For aliphatic alcohols, add a 2% concentration to disrupt phase separation.
For ammonium acetate, use either 50 or 100 mM concentrations.
